This changes the `FuncDef` from inside a helper that only builds a type, and it isn't needed. `prepare_method_signature` already sets `is_static` for every class-scope `__new__`, and the flag is serialized. I removed these two lines and the full `testcheck` suite still passed (6448 passed), and unannotated `__new__` still revealed the same types. As written, it also flags module-level or nested functions named `__new__` as static.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Making every `__new__` `is_static` breaks `dmypy suggest` on `__new__` methods. It now crashes where `main` returned a suggestion.

**Reviewed changes**

I reviewed the one commit that makes explicitly decorated `__new__` / `__init_subclass__` behave the same as the implicit forms. The issue's `@staticmethod def __new__(cls) -> Self` repro now type-checks cleanly. The new test fails on `main` and passes here, and the full `testcheck` suite passes.

- **`__new__` is now always static**: `prepare_method_signature` sets `is_static = True` on every `__new__`. The `cls` handling in `semanal`, `checker` and `typeops` is special-cased by name.
- **`checkmember` simplified**: instance member access now only checks `method.is_static` and no longer checks the `__new__` name.
- **`checker` `isclass` simplified**: the check drops the `__init_subclass__` name test and relies on semanal setting `is_class` for it.
- **New test `testSelfTypeNew_explicit`**: this is a decorated copy of `testSelfTypeNew`. Six fixtures also gain `classmethod` / `staticmethod` stubs.



### ⚠️ `dmypy suggest` crashes on `__new__`

`SuggestionEngine.get_suggestion` decides whether to skip the first argument with `is_method = bool(node.info) and not node.is_static`. Now that every `__new__` is static, `cls` is counted as a normal argument and indexing the call-site argument list runs past its end. I reproduced this: `dmypy suggest m.A.__new__` for `class A: def __new__(cls, x): ...` called as `A(1)` returns `(int) -> m.A` on `main`. On this branch the daemon crashes with `IndexError: list index out of range` at `mypy/suggestions.py:350`.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# dmypy suggest regression for `__new__`

## Affected sites
- mypy/suggestions.py:477 — `is_method = bool(node.info) and not node.is_static` is now False for every `__new__`, so `get_args` indexes `call.arg_types[i - is_method]` out of range (crash at mypy/suggestions.py:350).
- mypy/suggestions.py:704 — `if node.is_class or node.is_static:` now also strips the class name from `__new__` in `--json` (pyannotate) output. Before this PR, `__new__` kept its `A.__new__` qualified name.

## Required outcome
- `dmypy suggest <mod>.<Class>.__new__` produces the same suggestion as on `main`, e.g. `(int) -> m.A`.
- A regression test in `test-data/unit/fine-grained-suggest.test` that runs suggest on a `__new__` method.

## Suggested approach
- Use the same `(not node.is_static or node.name == "__new__")` idiom this PR applies elsewhere for `is_method`. Decide deliberately whether the pyannotate name-stripping at line 704 should change for `__new__`.
````

</details>

### ℹ️ Nitpicks

- The new test doesn't cover the issue's actual repro (`@staticmethod def __new__(cls) -> Self`) or an explicit `@classmethod __class_getitem__`, which the PR title mentions. Also, the `@classmethod __init_subclass__` half of the test already passes on `main`, so only the `__new__` half guards against this regression.
- The `classmethod` / `staticmethod` stubs added to `__init_subclass__.pyi`, `__new__.pyi`, `dict.pyi`, `object_with_init_subclass.pyi`, `primitives.pyi` and `tuple.pyi` are not used by any test in this PR. The new test uses `classmethod.pyi`, which already had both. Either add tests that need them or drop the fixture changes.
